articles.title: Elderly Palestinian woman killed, 19 wounded by Israeli violence in West Bank
articles.author: Aseel Saleh
articles.content_excerpt: Monday, November 16, marked another horrific night for Palestinians in the occupied West Bank after illegal Israeli settlers launched simultaneous assaults against civilians in the eastern governorate of Jericho, and the southern governorate of Bethlehem. Israeli settlers opened fire on Palestinian residents in Ad-Duyuk at-Tahta village west of Jericho, killing 72-year-old woman Fadda Fheidat and injuring 10 others. A relative of Fheidat told Palestine News and Information Agency WAFA , that the Israeli forces prohibited the family from holding a funeral procession in the village on Tuesday, November 17. articles.title: The US and Israel are inventing excuses for fresh escalation, says Iran
articles.author: Abdul Rahman
articles.content_excerpt: Iran has rejected reports about its possible involvement in planned attacks inside US cities, claiming them to be a part of a malicious campaign against the country waged to justify a possible new escalation in the US-Israeli war. “From the so-called ‘refrigerator cases’ in France to allegations that Iran is plotting to assassinate US officials, we are witnessing what appears to be a coordinated malign narrative campaign,” Esmail Baghaei, official spokesperson of Iran’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, pointed out in a post on X on Monday, November 16. After several supermarkets in France reported their fridges heating abnormally in October, its government claimed it was a result of a cyberattack and accused Iran for the same. His body was found with visible injuries, torn clothing and other signs of violence, raising suspicions that he had been tortured before being killed. articles.title: Hundreds of thousands reject Czech government’s media reform plans
articles.author: Ana Vračar
articles.content_excerpt: Hundreds of thousands of people gathered in Prague on Sunday, November 15, to protest against the Czech government’s plans to reform the financing model of public service media . The administration led by Prime Minister Andrej Babiš has pushed to replace the current license fee model for Czech Television and Czech Radio with direct financing from the state budget – a change critics fear would make the broadcasters more vulnerable to government pressure. articles.title: The victory of student populism
articles.author: Srđan Atanasovski
articles.content_excerpt: T he victory of the Student List in Serbia’s parliamentary elections on October 25, 2026 marks the end of fourteen years of domination by Aleksandar Vučić and his Serbian Progressive Party. With approximately 53 percent of the vote and a projected absolute majority in parliament, the Student List achieved a result that until recently had seemed almost unimaginable. The nature of this victory, and Serbia’s political future, are difficult to understand through the conventional categories of government versus opposition, liberalism versus conservatism, or European integration versus national sovereignty. articles.title: Bangladesh Faces Mounting Climate Crisis While Wealthy, Polluting Nations Resist Calls to Pay Up
articles.content_excerpt: Bangladesh’s first riverkeeper, Sharif Jamil, shares how poor countries in the Global South are struggling to effectively adapt to climate change as rising sea levels, extreme weather patterns, pollution and more are creating an escalating “humanitarian catastrophe,” while the wealthy impede efforts to reallocate financial resources for adaptation and mitigation. “If you want to protect the planet, if you want to save the planet from global warming, you need climate finance to make all this transition,” says Jamil.

articles.title: Senegal shipwreck adds to hundreds of migrant deaths at sea
articles.author: Nicholas Mwangi
articles.content_excerpt: The death toll from a migrant shipwreck off northwestern Senegal has risen to 43 , as search teams recovered more bodies along the coast near Loumpoul, between Dakar and Saint-Louis. Most of the dead were young people from nearby communities. It is the latest in a series of boat disasters that have killed more than 200 migrants on major migration routes over the past three months, as people trying to reach Europe and other destinations by sea continue to face deadly risks. On November 9, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) reported that at least 56 people had died in a series of shipwrecks off Senegal and Greece over the weekend. articles.title: There is only one Global South phrase for the APEC agenda: debt relief
articles.author: Vijay Prashad
articles.content_excerpt: In October, I visited a steel factory in Xinyu, Jiangxi province. There was no dust in the factory. At a desk, a woman wearing an orange hard hat monitored the production of silicon-steel strips. Her attention moved between the machinery and her keyboard. “Keep the belt at the proper speed,” she said. The precision of the process depended on her knowledge as much as on the equipment before her. Here was innovation at work, sustained by the skills of a worker. That scene stayed with me as I considered the forthcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen. articles.title: ASEAN summit in Manila met with protests over Trump’s participation
articles.author: Abdul Rahman
articles.content_excerpt: The 49th summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) opened in Manila, the Philippines on Sunday, November 15, amid large-scale protests against the presence of US President Donald Trump. Security forces clashed with protesters, injuring several and detaining hundreds, as they tried to march towards the Philippines International Convention Center. The protesters, carrying posters and banners with slogans against the US and Trump, the illegal war against Iran, and the proposed Pax Silica project in the country, tried to march to the venue of the summit despite police calling the protests illegal and erecting barricades to stop them.
